conclusions.rationale: The executable boundary, supported platforms, Windows console attachment, preserved flags and prohibited GUI/model side effects are explicit and observable; the read budget names hardware and release mode. This defines a feasible CLI branch before ordinary application startup, with platform regression proof still to be planned.

source_citations.excerpt: A `handy settings` invocation never shows a window, a tray icon or loads a model, never triggers the single-instance "show window" behavior, and completes reads within 2 seconds on an Apple M1 Mac in a release build.

conclusions.rationale: Read/discovery/scalar write behavior is explicit, including descriptor parsing, unknown keys, secret presence-only output, refusal of list/secret/read-only writes, equivalent JSON flag placement and a read-only missing-store path. Selecting the actual descriptor catalog is a legitimate technical plan decision.

source_citations.excerpt: `set` parses VALUE with the key's descriptor type (boolean `true`/`false`, integer, enumeration value, string). Generic `set` on a list key returns `validation_failed` naming the domain command to use; on a secret or read-only key it returns `validation_failed` stating that the key is changed in the settings UI.

conclusions.rationale: One backend validator is authoritative for both surfaces, with stable English errors, translated presentation and rejection replacing historical fallback. Rejected writes preserve settings. Tests can use the same value matrix through UI commands and CLI rather than duplicate validators.

source_citations.excerpt: Every write goes through the same backend validation functions as the corresponding UI command, so a value the UI rejects is rejected by the CLI with the same error code and English message, and vice versa; the UI may show that message translated.

conclusions.rationale: The revision contract distinguishes actual changes from no-ops and reads, covers every writer, defines conflict detail location and requires locked reread before patching. The concurrency scenario and SC-002 provide a falsifiable lost-update oracle. Cross-process locking and atomic store replacement remain implementation choices.

source_citations.excerpt: All writers (UI commands, a running instance and a headless CLI process) are serialized by one cross-process settings lock, and each writer re-reads the stored settings under that lock before applying its change, so a write without expected revision applies to the latest settings and never discards fields changed by another writer.

conclusions.rationale: Identity is scoped to the same user and settings store; live routing, timeout with unknown outcome, older-version refusal and headless fallback are all explicit. No-answer never authorizes another writer. User-only permissions and no network listener constrain the transport; its concrete per-platform mechanism belongs in the plan.

source_citations.excerpt: If no answer arrives in time, the CLI returns `unavailable` with `error.details.outcome` set to `unknown`, and agents must read again before retrying. If a running Handy without this channel (an older version) is detected, the CLI returns `unavailable` and never writes the store itself.

conclusions.rationale: The foundation owns the shared parsing/input/dry-run/commit/help framework and existing output settings. New smart paste and automatic Enter belong to later owner features, and help must match the actual build. Clarifications resolve the replacement/destination examples as downstream scenarios with a test-only fixture for 008.

source_citations.excerpt: The domains microphones, replacements, vocabulary, shortcuts, prompts, destination and the new output settings (smart paste method, automatic Enter) are added on this framework by the features that own them (001–007, 009, 010).

conclusions.rationale: The success/failure envelope, mandatory object details, separation of stderr and stdout and special export behavior are sufficiently exact to parse and snapshot. Human-readable text remains presentation freedom without weakening the machine contract.

source_citations.excerpt: Diagnostics, warnings and progress go to stderr in both modes. Export operations writing to `-` print only the exported content without `--json`, and put it in `data.content` of the envelope with `--json`.

conclusions.rationale: The complete mapping of named errors to exits is explicit, preserves existing meanings and reserves additive codes. SC-003 distinguishes foundation-owned tests from later domain-owned errors, avoiding a requirement to implement absent domains.

source_citations.excerpt: Error codes and exit codes are stable and documented: `usage_error` and `validation_failed`, `shortcut_conflict`, `limit_exceeded` → 2; `revision_conflict` → 3; `not_found` → 4; `unavailable` → 5; `persistence_failed` and `internal_error` → 1; success → 0.

conclusions.rationale: The functional CLI boundary directly references AC-001, which defines preserved flags and observable headless behavior across all platforms. No incompatible stack replacement or unrelated feature is required.

source_citations.excerpt: Add a `settings` subcommand group to the existing executable that runs without GUI side effects and keeps existing flags unchanged.

conclusions.rationale: Get, keys and scalar set are grounded in AC-002 with secret redaction and explicit refusal boundaries. The descriptor entity provides a technical discovery contract and Stories 1/2 provide usable behavioral tests.

source_citations.excerpt: Provide generic get, keys and set operations over non-secret settings with redaction of secrets.

conclusions.rationale: The service explicitly unifies UI and CLI validation/commit and carries lock/revision semantics expanded in AC-003 and AC-004. The requirement includes internal writes through AC-004, so the plan must inventory all existing writer paths rather than merely new CLI code.

source_citations.excerpt: Expose one shared validation and commit service used by UI commands and CLI, with a persisted revision, optional expected-revision check and a single write lock.

conclusions.rationale: Live routing or headless application is a clear mutually constrained behavior with a user-only channel and bounded timeout. AC-005 adds required old-version and unknown-outcome safety, preventing silent fallback into concurrent writers.

source_citations.excerpt: Route CLI operations to a running instance over a user-only local channel with a 5-second timeout, or apply them headlessly when no instance runs.

conclusions.rationale: The framework API capability is defined without prematurely shipping all domains. AC-006 and Clarifications allocate ownership and prescribe fixture-only tests for domains not yet delivered; extensions can reuse the foundation without violating ordering.

source_citations.excerpt: Provide the domain command framework (file/stdin input, dry run, atomic commit, help) used by features 001–007, 009 and 010.

conclusions.rationale: AC-007 and AC-008 define the exact observable JSON/stream/error/exit behaviors that this functional requirement references. Stories 1 and 5 and SC-003 give an automated parsing and exit-status oracle.

source_citations.excerpt: Produce the documented JSON envelope, human output, stderr diagnostics, stable error codes and exit codes.

conclusions.rationale: The 100% criterion is measurable against the descriptor inventory of settable keys. AC-003 makes both accept/reject decisions and English error reasons comparable; secret/read-only keys are explicit refusal paths rather than hidden settable exceptions.

source_citations.excerpt: Parity tests show identical accept/reject decisions and reasons between UI commands and CLI for 100% of settable keys.

conclusions.rationale: Zero lost committed fields and refusal of every stale expected revision are falsifiable with deliberately interleaved writers and deterministic scheduling. AC-004 defines locked reread and revision increments so the test has an exact state oracle.

source_citations.excerpt: In concurrency tests with interleaved UI and CLI writers, zero committed fields are lost and every stale expected revision is refused.

conclusions.rationale: Every foundation-owned error must occur in an automated test with its documented exit code; later domain errors have separate owners. Injected persistence/internal/channel failures can make all named outcomes testable without requiring runtime accidents.

source_citations.excerpt: Every error code owned by this feature (`usage_error`, `validation_failed`, `revision_conflict`, `not_found`, `unavailable`, `persistence_failed`, `internal_error`) is produced by at least one automated test with its documented exit code; domain codes (`shortcut_conflict`, `limit_exceeded`) are tested by the features that own them.

findings.description: The spec promises rejection changes nothing and live writes re-register shortcuts. Partial failure of registration or persistence must not leave the runtime and persisted configuration divergent; this is a technical rollback risk not resolved by merely sharing validation.

findings.description: The current implementation is described as per-command whole-settings writes without a lock, while AC-004 extends the new revision/lock protocol to Handy internal writes. Missing any writer would invalidate the concurrency guarantee even if CLI-only tests pass.
